bounded_findings: Native SystemUI constrains some Hebrew notification-header metadata and the Hebrew speaker-on action label. The new missed-call notifications keep readable caller names, single/multiple titles and Clear; their phone-number suffix is ellipsized.

Contacts/recents show the fixed keypad button overlapping a lower row dial control at the captured scroll offset. Some lower rows are partial above fixed navigation. Long names and date/time metadata are ellipsized. Upper controls, selected shapes, tabs and summaries remain readable; scroll recovery and actual dialing require separate native evidence.
Icon chooser captures show opposite clipped endpoints of the scrollable list. Complementary bottom captures expose the final options; Cancel remains visible.
Some narrow widget previews ellipsize a long contact name or the DA CALLER header. Hebrew initials, other shown names and selected shapes remain legible.
Compact English and real-call caller labels may ellipsize; expanded caller identity remains available.
Actual Main compact mode floating dial button can overlap part of a lower row, recoverable by scrolling; expanded mode hides it and retains at least one visible row. Long row names/dates ellipsize.
Native incoming notification short header ellipsizes while caller body and action buttons remain readable.
scope_limits: All101 call-design captures are static fictional call-state fixtures rendered by the production in-app call UI. This visual inspection does not establish real Telecom action acknowledgement or actual audible routing.

The pictured coverage includes five call designs, light/dark variants, normal/audio/more/keypad states, Hebrew/English long names, font scale1.3 and an English no-Bluetooth output chooser. It does not exhaust every possible font, data, theme and device combination.
This visual review does not test a physical Jelly Star, SIM/carrier calls, microphone/speaker/Bluetooth audio, lockscreen/proximity, full TalkBack or a matching-key data-preserving upgrade.
